name: AgFunder: agrifoodtech funding data and AI portfolio examples
title: AgFunder: agrifoodtech funding data and AI portfolio examples
answer: AgFunder is a venture capital firm whose website combines agrifoodtech funding figures, portfolio case studies and research notes. Its most useful contribution for AI in agriculture is a funding barometer: global agrifoodtech raised $16 billion in 2024, just 4% below 2023, after a 49% fall to $15.6 billion in 2023. The site also profiles AI-linked companies such as Aigen's autonomous weeding robots, AI Palette's big-data product innovation platform and Root AI's greenhouse harvesting robots.

sections.body: AgFunder publishes this website as a venture capital firm focused on agrifood, human and planetary health investing. The pages read include the homepage, portfolio case studies for AI Palette and Root AI, and a research article on emerging versus established venture capital fund formation. The site presents agrifoodtech funding figures for 2023 and 2024, describes portfolio companies and their technologies, and discusses venture fund structures. It does not present itself as a peer-reviewed or independent statistical publication.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AgFunder states that AI is its fabric and that it hired an engineering team before most venture capital firms to help identify entrepreneurs and technologies. On funding, it reports that global agrifoodtech showed signs of recovery in 2024, reaching $16 billion, a 4% drop from 2023. It also says the food and agriculture technology market raised $15.6 billion in 2023, a 49% year-over-year decline, while the broader venture capital market fell 38% in 2023. The portfolio pages describe AI-linked companies. Aigen makes small autonomous weeding robots to minimize chemical use. AI Palette, a Singapore-based company founded in 2018, is developing a cloud-based SaaS platform that uses big-data analytics to scan millions of data points across multiple geographies and languages, tracking local and migrating flavor trends; the page says new FMCG products have a failure rate of at least 85%, translating into annual losses of up to $40 billion for big food and beverage brands. Root AI makes autonomous robots for greenhouse harvesting, with its first robot focused on cherry tomato picking and plans to move cross crop before 2021; it converted several memoranda of understanding to paid contracts ahead of schedule, partly because Covid-19 put pressure on greenhouse labor. The research article says emerging fund managers are finding opportunities while established funds struggle, that alignment and specialization matter more than track record and platform scale, and that deep tech managers with technical backgrounds are launching focused funds in AI, climate technology and biotech.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: AgFunder reports $16 billion in global agrifoodtech funding in 2024, a 4% drop from 2023, and $15.6 billion in 2023, a 49% year-over-year decline, against a 38% fall in the broader venture capital market in 2023. It says new FMCG products have a failure rate of at least 85%, causing annual losses of up to $40 billion for big food and beverage brands. It notes AI Palette was founded in 2018 in Singapore and Root AI planned to move cross crop before 2021. It describes the 2% management fee and 20% carry model as strained and says emerging managers are experimenting with lower management fees, higher carry, equity participation in management companies and performance fees tied to milestones, and building more concentrated portfolios instead of the traditional 20-30 investment power law strategy.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in agriculture can use AgFunder as a funding barometer and a source of concrete company examples. The funding figures show the direction of capital into agrifoodtech after a sharp decline, while the portfolio pages show where AI is being applied: autonomous weeding, greenhouse harvesting and big-data product innovation for food brands. The research article adds context on how specialist deep tech funds focused on AI are being formed, which helps explain who may finance the next wave of agricultural AI. The site is useful for tracking investment flow and commercial use cases rather than for technical benchmarks or independent field trials.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: AgFunder is a venture capital firm, so its portfolio pages are selective and promotional by nature, and several companies are marked exited or exit. The funding figures are presented without a full methodology on the pages read. The research article concerns venture fund formation broadly, not agriculture AI specifically, and it is based on insights from a Women in VC/PE conference. The site does not provide independent validation, detailed model performance, farm-level trial results or regulatory guidance for AI in agriculture.
